messages:
elaine: Heads up — hosted API (us-west-2) is spiking 5xx/504s since 09:02. I can see a big jump in cache evictions and a bunch of redis timeouts in the logs. Anyone oncall?
incidents-bot: ALERT: gateway.5xx_rate ↑ 8x in us-west-2. telemetry: cache.evictions/sec ↑ 12x, redis.conn_errors ↑ 60. Affected route: /v1/generate.
samir: I'm on it. Pulling up metrics now — RPS steady, but prefix-cache evictions shot up. Looks like a TTL/eviction storm rather than traffic surge.
maya: We shipped the "prefix-ttl-weight" change at 08:50 to improve cache turnover. Could that have misbehaved and caused mass expiry?
samir: Very likely. Also seeing many Redis replies: "IOERR: read error" and "ERR maxmemory" in the node logs. Sample trace: `2024-02-27T09:03:11Z redis-02: io timeout GET prefix:abc123`
support-ivy: Customers reporting timeouts on /v1/generate. Example correlation id: abc12345 -> gateway returned 504 after 30s. Several enterprise tenants hit errors.
samir: Quick mitigation plan: 1) rollback prefix-ttl-weight, 2) enable memcached fallback for hot prefixes, 3) temporarily increase redis maxmemory on the affected shard. I'll run steps 1+2 now.
maya: Rolling back the change (config-repo PR #412) and triggering rollout. ETA ~45s for config to propagate.
samir: Enabling memcached fallback in routing rules (patching route-config) — switching hot prefixes to fallback pool to reduce pressure on Redis. Also increasing redis maxmemory by 15% via infra API.
incidents-bot: ACTION: rollback config merged by maya. | config-propagation: started | routing-change: samir | infra-change: redis scale up requested
samir: After routing and memcached fallback, 5xx rate dropping — gateway.5xx_rate back down ~2x baseline, evictions tapering. Still seeing some 504s for long requests.
elaine: Good work. Can we confirm customers affected and start outreach? Ivy, can you draft?
support-ivy: On it. I'll pull a list from the error logs (correlation ids) and start customer pings.
maya: Need follow-up: make prefix-ttl-weight change gated with canary and smaller ramp. Also add a pre-deploy test for eviction rate on staging.
samir: Agreed. I'll open a runbook PR with explicit mitigation steps (memcached fallback + redis memory bump) and add an alert run condition for eviction spikes.
elaine: Postmortem owners: samir (mitigation timeline + runbook), maya (config change + deployment gating), ivy (customer comms). Add timeline and RCA in incidents board. :thumbsup:
samir: Final note — keep routing fallback enabled for 1 hour while infra stabilizes, then revert. Monitoring: watch redis.conn_errors and cache.evictions/sec closely.
support-ivy: Customer pings sent for top 3 tenants, we're offering incident summary + ETA.
elaine: Last check in — error rates back to normal ranges at 09:14. Closing active response, leaving tasks open for postmortem.
